recipes.name: Rempel Family Meatloaf
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Stir the ground beef, crushed crackers, Cheddar cheese, and onion soup mix in a large bowl until well combined. Whisk the eggs, ketchup, and steak sauce in a separate bowl until smooth. Mix the eggs into the meat until evenly combined, if the mixture seems too dry, add a little water. Press into a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Bake in preheated oven until the meatloaf reaches 160 degrees F (71 degrees C) and is no longer pink in the center, 45 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rempel Family Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Meatloaf with cheese, onion soup mix, steak sauce and crushed buttery round crackers.

review.reviewBody: Oh my this is good! Hubby can't stand any sort of meatloaf. Until now! He LOVED this which says quite a lot. I doubled it and we still didn't have a lot leftover for sandwiches. He piled his plate high! I made mashed potatoes and green peas to go with it. Tip for cutting the grease: put several pieces of sandwich bread underneath the meatloaf. It will soak up a lot of the grease, then just throw the nasty greasy bread away when the loaf is done! Thank you Rempels for sharing your recipe!!!!

I am on a perpetual search for a good meatloaf recipe, have tried many, and my hubby and I really like this one. It is good for making meatloaf burgers, too! Just add about 1/4 more cracker crumbs to make the burgers firmer. Plus, a good glaze for the meatloaf is 3T ketchup, 1T honey and 1/2t worchestershire. Pour it on before baking and you've got yourself one GOOD meatloaf!

I have made this recipe twice now and it is really a taste treat. This last time, I added 1/2 cup ketchup, a little finely chopped green pepper, and a few extra crackers. I saved a little of the ketchup mixture and topped the meatloaf with it during the last 1/2 hour of baking. I served it to company and was asked for a copy of the recipe so they could make it too. Thanks for the great recipe Connie.

So good!! I wish I had leftovers!! I made two pans last night for a dinner party (7 people) and by the end there was absolutley no meatloaf left!! I took the advice of Mrs. Rempel her self and used 3/4 chedder cheese and 1/4 mozzarella and I also used Cheez-its insted of butter crackers. I sifted the onion soup mix and added only the flakes and a few pinches of the powder. I made the glaze recommend by KINZ: 3T ketchup, 1T honey and 1/2t worchestershire. I poured it over the meat before backing and it made one amazing meatloaf!!

When I remarried, we made a deal: I would do the cooking and my wife would do the dishes. I don't like meatloaf, my wife did. I don't make meatloaf. My wife would volunteer to cook so she could make meatloaf. I would have to use salsa to cover the flavor so I could eat it. Then my wife's ALS progressed and she couldn’t cook or do dishes. I found this recipe and made it for my wife. Surprise! Surprise! Surprise! I like this meatloaf, as is, no salsa, no extras required. Today, lacking “buttery round crackers” I did something new. I made the recipe minus the crackers and used only one egg, formed meatballs, placed them on parchment paper on a grilling rack, set the pellet smoker at 180, and a few hours later . . . Dang near addictive meatballs.

My family loves this meatloaf. It is our favorite. I like to use cheeze its or cheesy ritz crackers. I also add in some Worcestershire to my ketchup mix and garlic, Cajun seasoning, pepper, Montreal and onion powder to my meat in addition to the other ingredients listed in the recipe. This is the only meatloaf we make. I also make a glaze to go on top 1/4 cup ketchup, 2 TBSP light brown sugar and 1 TBSP red wine vinegar. I add it on the last 15 minutes before it's done. Thank you for an amazing recipe!!
I used crushed pork rinds instead of crackers . No steak sauce but Worchester sauce and brown sugar in topping. I microwaved it for 4 minutes or so and browned it under the broiler for a few minutes.

Thanks for the recipe! We love it and agree with others never enough leftovers. This is our go to meatloaf hands down. I follow the recipe adding only about 1/4 cup of breadcrumbs to round it out. Additionally, because I usually cook it on a Sunday for a weekday meal, I slice it thick, spray with olive oil and bake 10-15 minutes flipping once. Each piece gets a fabulous crunchy crust on it.

Delicious. This is a good recipe. My kids love meatloaf but this is the ticket at the end of a long work day. This recipe is quick and easy. I made a ketchup, brown sugar, Worcester sauce glaze for the second half of baking.

My husband has always liked my meatloaf so I thought I would just give this a try. He loves it even more. Been making this one for several years now. I don't do the bread on the bottom. Tired it and we didn't like how it turned out. I just drain it really well if I use a loaf pan. Or I have often free-formed the loaf so it's crispy all around. I spay a broiler pan and set it on a lipped pan so that the grease flows to the bottom. I have even not used the broiler pan and cooked potatoes and carrots around it and then just drain them when done. Also have started using extra sharp or triple cheddar cheese. Also always uses Worcestershire. But have kept the eggs and even used one more for binding. Otherwise, it falls apart. We don't care as it still takes great. I have also kept the ketchup the same too. But I always add garlic and onion powder as we love both. The dry soup mix I have used beefy mushroom and the onion one and liked both.

Best meatloaf I ever made!! I didn’t have any Lipton dry soup so I made my own and Instead of beef bullion granules I substituted dry Aujus mix. Used sharp cheddar cheese. The only addition I made was for a topping on the meatloaf. I mixed 1/4 cup each of brown sugar and ketchup. The last 15 minutes I poured that on meatloaf. This will be our go to meatloaf now! My husband hates leftovers but he wanted meatloaf sandwiches for lunch today!!

I skip the cheese now, because it was nearly indiscernible. I also use bread crumbs, rather than the crackers to eliminate some sodium (plus I think they are sweet). The Bobbly Flay meatloaf balsamic glaze is fantastic on this!
Excellent flavors.
I left out the steak sauce. Delicious
I've personally never cared much for meatloaf but we all love this recipe. I add a glaze before putting it in the oven... combine a 1/2 cup of both brown sugar and ketchup and brush over top. Yum!!

This is now my go to meatloaf. I make 2 loaves (3 lb of meat) since it disappears so quickly. I only use 1 packet of onion soup and just about a tablespoon of ketchup for both. So tasty! I need to make 2 loaves for my small family so we have leftovers for sandwiches!

I doubled the recipe to 3lbs, but that was the only alteration made. I was hoping mine would end up looking like the picture of the meatloaf n with cheese marbled throughout, but it didn't. I used thinly shredded cheddar cheese, so maybe that was a factor. Either way, it was very tasty. I think next time I'll try velveeta or Harvati.
some small tweaks, bbq sauce instead of ketchup, meatloaf mix packet instead of soup mix, meatloaf mix (or pork). layer of meat - bbq sauce - cheese and top with hashbrowns.
A little dry but good!
This meat loaf brings all the boys to the yard.
